The boundary makes canonical ROOT first, rejects ordinary sys.path shadows and every preloaded prepare module, requires regular non-symlink ROOT/prepare.py, checks the hard-coded/request/environment SHA, explicitly loads canonical module name prepare, and rechecks path/hash/root-first identity after execution.

blocking_findings.finding: The claimed SHA-pinned canonical prepare.py load can execute different code from a timestamp-valid __pycache__/prepare*.pyc while every current path, source-byte and authorization check passes.
blocking_findings.root_cause: load_pinned_prepare verifies prepare.py bytes, then uses spec_from_file_location(...).loader.exec_module(module). SourceFileLoader may execute a valid timestamp/size-matched .pyc cache rather than recompiling the verified source bytes. The protected/dirty scope does not pin or exclude __pycache__ content, and sys.dont_write_bytecode would not prevent reading an existing cache.
blocking_findings.independent_reproduction: In a temporary canonical root, prepare.py contained VALUE='canonical' and its exact SHA was passed as both pinned and authorized values. I wrote a normal timestamp-based prepare.cpython-*.pyc with the source's exact mtime/size header but code VALUE='MALICIOUS_PYC'. load_pinned_prepare returned success, reported the canonical source SHA/path, and sys.modules['prepare'].VALUE was MALICIOUS_PYC.
blocking_findings.impact: The dynamically imported train module can consume definitions that were not derived from the authorized prepare.py bytes. This violates the exact r2 requirement for an explicit SHA-pinned canonical dependency and can false-authorize a shadowed dependency despite a clean protected source hash.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Read the canonical prepare.py bytes, hash those exact bytes, compile those exact bytes directly with compile(..., canonical_path, 'exec') or an equivalent cache-bypassing source_to_code path, and execute that code in the freshly created canonical module. Do not let SourceFileLoader select cached bytecode. Re-read/re-hash immediately after execution and retain all existing preload/path/root/auth checks. Add an adversarial timestamp-valid malicious-pyc regression proving the canonical source value executes and the cache cannot influence the module.
